title: Ivo and the Postcard
premise: Marine biologist Juniper Whitlock has spent ten years avoiding her hometown of Salt Hollow, where a single unsent postcard and an unspoken confession still sit between her and Eli Marchetti, the boy she loved and left. When a freak snowstorm traps her in the town's shuttered aquarium with Eli — and with Calla, the rival who once chose ambition over friendship and now returns seeking forgiveness — old wounds force all three to confront the mistake that scattered their found family. As Juniper counts nesting turtles through the storm's aftermath, she discovers the postcard was never lost, only hidden, and that Eli has been waiting not for an apology but for her sentence, finally spoken: 'I should have stayed.' The novel ends with Juniper choosing to remain in Salt Hollow, rebuilding both the aquarium and the family she once abandoned.
about_author: Kestrel Whitlock is the pen name of a former tide-pool docent who writes love stories set in small coastal towns where everyone remembers everything. She lives within walking distance of the ocean and insists this is research.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In the Florida Keys, Juniper logs sea turtle nests with mechanical precision, counting turtles instead of heartbreaks. A grant letter arrives offering funding for the failing Salt Hollow Aquarium — her hometown, her past. Emotional beat: avoidance dressed as ambition; she accepts before she can talk herself out of it.

chapters.title: Salt Hollow Smells Like 2014
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She drives into town after ten years away, recognizing every landmark and dreading one building on Harbor Street. Her aunt Ruthie offers tea and pointed silence about Eli Marchetti. Emotional beat: the vertigo of returning; grief disguised as nostalgia.

chapters.title: The Man Behind the Counter
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli runs the hardware store his father left him, steady and unreadable, when Juniper walks in needing epoxy resin for the aquarium tanks. Ten years compress into four minutes of small talk. Emotional beat: shock held under glass; neither says what matters.

chapters.title: Grant Conditions
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The grant requires community partnership signatures by December 21st — including the aquarium board, which Eli chairs. Forced proximity begins. Emotional beat: resentment curdling into reluctant respect as she sees how much he's done for the town.

chapters.title: Calla Comes Home
chapters.summary: Calla's POV. Calla Reyes arrives from Seattle, famous now, carrying a donation check and a decade of guilt over choosing a fellowship abroad the night their friend group shattered. She wants to fund the aquarium and be forgiven. Emotional beat: hope braided with dread; she knows she isn't welcome.

chapters.title: Three at a Table
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Ruthie engineers a dinner seating all three rivals-turned-strangers. Old stories surface, then old accusations. Calla leaves early; Eli drives her home without a word to Juniper. Emotional beat: the past is not past; it's load-bearing.

chapters.title: What the Storm Warning Said
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Forecasters predict a once-in-a-decade snowstorm. The aquarium's generator is failing and the rehabbed turtles need heat. Eli volunteers to stay overnight; so does Juniper; so does Calla, arriving with supplies. Emotional beat: duty as an excuse to be trapped together.

chapters.title: Snowed In
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Roads close by midnight. Three adults, one aquarium, no exits. They patch the generator by flashlight, laughing despite themselves, and the old rhythm of their twenties flickers alive. Emotional beat: dangerous warmth; muscle memory of friendship.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake of Our Twenties
chapters.summary: Calla's POV. By candlelight, Calla finally tells her version of the night everything broke — the night Juniper left without saying goodbye and Eli burned the group's shared photo album. Truths collide; each remembers it differently. Emotional beat: catharsis weaponized; honesty that wounds.

chapters.title: The Postcard
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Hunting for blankets, Juniper finds a locked drawer in Eli's office — inside, the postcard she wrote him ten years ago and never sent, creased from being read hundreds of times. He kept it. He read it. He never answered. Emotional beat: devastation and revelation entwined.

chapters.title: Why You Never Sent It
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Confronted, Eli admits he found the postcard years ago in a returned-mail box and couldn't answer a sentence that began 'I should have' and ended nowhere. 'You never finished it,' he says. Emotional beat: the cruelest cliffhanger of the heart; a sentence missing its ending.

chapters.title: Turtle Watch
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Dawn breaks over snow-covered water. Juniper checks the cold-stunned turtles, and Eli joins her, hands working beside hers like no time passed. They don't speak of the postcard, but something has shifted. Emotional beat: tenderness re-entering through work, not words.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Ledger
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Ruthie reveals family history: Whitlocks have always run from Salt Hollow and always come back, and there's a reason Juniper's mother never did. Juniper learns her leaving wasn't cowardice alone — it was inheritance. Emotional beat: compassion for her younger self; identity reframed.

chapters.title: Calla's Confession, Continued
chapters.summary: Calla's POV. Calla tells Juniper privately why she really took the fellowship: she was running from feelings for Eli she thought were safer than friendship, and choosing the job was choosing not to choose. Emotional beat: rivalry dissolving into mutual recognition of two women who fled the same heart.

chapters.title: The Board Meeting
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. The grant board convenes; Calla's donation plus Juniper's grant could save the aquarium permanently — if Eli signs the partnership. He hesitates, fearing permanence means watching Juniper leave again. Emotional bet: commitment as terror; the signature he can't give.

chapters.title: Almost the Sentence
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. On the harbor seawall, Juniper starts the sentence — 'I should have stayed because' — and a truck backfires, a gull screams, Eli's phone rings. Interruption after interruption. She retreats. Emotional beat: agonizing near-miss; timing as antagonist.

chapters.title: News From the Keys
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper's old mentor calls: the dream job in the Keys is hers if she starts in January. The escape hatch opens exactly when staying becomes possible. Emotional beat: the old pattern offering itself like a warm bath; temptation with a salary.

chapters.title: Eli Lets Go
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli hears about the offer and, loving her more than his own hope, tells her to take it. 'You always belonged to bigger water.' He signs the partnership papers and withdraws. Emotional beat: sacrifice mistaken for peace; the quietest heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Empty Tank
chapters.summary: Calla's POV. Calla finds Juniper staring at the emptied quarantine tank, the turtles released, nothing left to count. Calla delivers the novel's turn: 'You keep waiting for better timing. There is no better timing. There's just the sentence.' Emotional beat: found family doing its truest work.

chapters.title: I Should Have Stayed
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the harbor, in falling snow, Juniper finds Eli locking up the aquarium and says the whole sentence at last: 'I should have stayed. I'm asking to stay now.' He doesn't answer with words. Emotional beat: climax; a decade of rehearsal spent in nine words.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The three rebuild the aquarium together — Calla funding, Eli building, Juniper directing rehabilitation. Calla forgives herself; Eli forgives the album; Juniper declines the Keys by mail. Emotional beat: repair made visible; family chosen twice.

chapters.title: Postmarked, Finally
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. One year later, Juniper mails the original postcard to Eli from three streets away, having written the missing ending beneath her old unfinished line. He reads it on their porch. Last image: two names on a mailbox, turtles in the tank, home. Emotional beat: resolution; the sentence completed, the circle closed.
